title: EMMA: Structured Episodic Memory for Multi-Agent Workflow Synthesis
abstract: arXiv:2610.35966v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Deploying LLM agents in specialized domains often require fine-grained task-specific procedures and knowledge a general model lacks, yet parameter training is costly and non-interpretable, and hand-engineered agent systems shift the cost to expert labor. Episodic memory updates at context level, but single agent adaptation struggles to alleviate cross-task interference, especially with complex tasks such as multi-application navigation or data pool analysis. Although multi-agent evolution alleviates this problem, existing methods lack clear definitions on update rules and rely on the backbone model to decide where and how much the system changes. This ill-scoped evolution makes learning follow the backbone's structural preferences rather than the observed failures: one backbone accumulates skills while another spawns agents. translated_title: EMMA：面向多智能体工作流合成的结构化情景记忆
translated_abstract: 在专业领域部署LLM智能体通常需要通用模型所缺乏的细粒度任务特定程序和知识，然而参数训练成本高昂且不可解释，而手工设计的智能体系统则将成本转嫁给专家人力。情景记忆虽然在上下文层面进行更新，但单智能体自适应难以缓解跨任务干扰，尤其是在多应用导航或数据池分析等复杂任务中。尽管多智能体演化缓解了这一问题，但现有方法缺乏对更新规则的清晰定义，而是依赖骨干模型来决定系统在何处以及以多大程度进行改变。这种范围界定不清的演化使得学习遵循骨干模型的结构偏好而非观测到的失败：某些骨干模型倾向于积累技能，而另一些则倾向于生成智能体。我们提出了EMMA（面向多智能体工作流合成的结构化情景记忆），该方法将配置……
tldr: 提出了EMMA框架，通过结构化情景记忆进行多智能体工作流合成，解决了单智能体自适应中的跨任务干扰问题，以及现有多智能体演化方法中更新规则不清、变化范围依赖骨干模型偏好而非实际失败经验的问题。
en_tdlr: EMMA introduces structured episodic memory for multi-agent workflow synthesis, addressing cross-task interference in single-agent adaptation and the ill-scoped evolution problem where existing methods follow backbone structural preferences rather than observed failures.
